01 / About

Engineering practice.
Research perspective.

I translate questions about facility behaviour, system stability, and emerging technologies into engineering requirements, assessment methods, and research.

I am a Principal Power System Engineer at the Independent Electricity System Operator (IESO), where I lead technical work on large computational loads and their integration into Ontario’s power system.

Since 2016, I have held an Assistant Professor appointment in the Department of Electrical Power and Machines at Ain Shams University, currently on approved leave while based in Canada. IESO is my primary employer.

Across industry and academia, I focus on understanding physical behaviour, testing assumptions, and communicating the evidence behind engineering decisions.

2026–present · Canada

Earlier IESO engineering roles
August 2013–2026

My experience spans connection assessments, dynamic studies, technical requirements, and operating limits for generation, battery storage, transmission, and large loads.

  • Lead development of technical requirements for large computational loads, covering ride-through, restoration, demand variability, ramping, oscillations, monitoring, and modelling.
  • Conduct and guide reliability studies using PSS/E, PSCAD, and PowerTech DSA.
  • Coordinate engineering perspectives across connection stakeholders and mentor engineers on model assumptions, study interpretation, and reliability evidence.
  • Contributed to Lakeshore Transmission Station Integration and updates to the Ontario Resource and Transmission Assessment Criteria.

03 / Research

A changing grid.
Connected research questions.

Power-system physics and computational methods, grounded in the demands of emerging energy infrastructure.

01

Data centres &
large-load integration

Investigating how data-centre controls, UPS systems, and battery storage affect grid stability and continuity of critical computing loads.

Ride-through · Frequency response · Oscillation damping

02

AI for power-system
assessment & control

Studying machine-learning methods for power flow, dynamic-security assessment, and control, with attention to physical consistency, uncertainty, and safety constraints.

Learning-based control · Security assessment · Power flow

03

Hydrogen &
integrated energy systems

Examining the grid-connection behaviour of hydrogen hubs and co-located computing, hydrogen production, and storage across multiple timescales.

Hydrogen hubs · Coupled loads · Connection requirements

04

Renewable
generation

Research foundations in photovoltaic-array reconfiguration, partial-shading losses, and wind-generator fault response.

PV reconfiguration · Renewable integration · Fault response
